title: Who ordered the extra cake?
brief: The first customer asks for cake. The next customer orders the regular lunch, but cake appears on their receipt too. A fresh service works perfectly. Follow the two requests and find what crossed the counter.
objective: Locate the function that lets one customer's request change another customer's menu. Explain why the existing copy does not prevent it.

provenance.origin: An original RepoQuest teaching fixture. The cafe and incident are fictional; the Python behavior and captured test failures are reproducible. This is not a third-party historical bug.

hints.text: Compare a fresh service with two requests handled by the same service. Which object survives both requests?
The outer dictionary is copied. Follow the value stored under items: does the code create another list?
Appending the special mutates the list shared with the cached menu. Each returned menu needs its own items list before anything is appended.

solution.text: dict.copy() copies the outer dictionary but retains the same items list. Appending cake changes the cached list, so later customers inherit it; previously returned menus also change. The patch copies the items list for each request. That is sufficient for this fixture because its items are immutable strings; it is not a general deep-copy guarantee. The unchanged behavior contract checks both later and earlier customers.
